findings_and_qualified_observations.classification: independent current source confirmation of prior conditional concern, not a new unique finding
findings_and_qualified_observations.historical_owner: 059 queue entry 1868, Q-L12-70fe8fdc0c143bb1aa06, reports direct longitude interpolation could take long way if actual supported route crosses antimeridian; bounded prior web-map geographic rectangles exclude crossing
findings_and_qualified_observations.observation: Both web and server calculate spherical lengths, then interpolate longitude directly. Endpoints near +179.9° and -179.9° at equal latitude represent a short spherical arc but a halfway arithmetic interpolation is near 0° rather than ±180°. This is mathematical reasoning from source, not a runtime fixture. The shown validator checks WGS84, segment and endpoint constraints but no seam check in its inspected body. The server result feeds camp-foraging coordinates and exposure position, and web result feeds camp vicinity or replanning origin.
findings_and_qualified_observations.condition: Requires an admitted and persisted route whose actual segment crosses the longitude seam and an intermediate movement minute. Inspect actual regional terrain/producer and supported geography before asserting product reachability; earlier regional-bounds sources explicitly exclude crossing rectangles. No runtime consequence measured.
findings_and_qualified_observations.future_repair_direction: Decide supported seam/geodesic policy and coordinate both server and web interpolation owners; if crossing is supported, use a shared correct wrapped interpolation while preserving endpoint order, units, movement timing and native boundary conversions. If excluded, make that invariant explicit at authoritative admission. Do not implement now.

findings_and_qualified_observations.observation: Generated JourneyRoutePoint has public raw i32 axes; the first-party route-view conversion carries the vector unchanged. The web reader checks axes and expects success, so a retained invalid point visited by the reader would panic. The shown planned-route validator rejects any out-of-range point and selected reducers invoke it, and this is a material qualification to hypothetical unsafe-input reachability.
findings_and_qualified_observations.condition: No malformed retained row, bypassing writer, SDK fault, unchecked product input, or panic has been observed. The full writer and storage-integrity graph remains open; one-point/zero-minute example belongs to the older finding and is not evidence that its normal admission path permits it.
findings_and_qualified_observations.future_repair_direction: Trace every authoritative writer and readmission; own checked route coordinate at the accepted boundary or propagate a typed failure through the web reader. Generated SDK bindings are read-only evidence; a future schema change would update schema and generated clients through the repository workflow, not hand-edit this file.

findings_and_qualified_observations.classification: prior 774 Root-extra40 F001/F002 as named by Native lower-dependency qualifier, current same-body corroboration only
findings_and_qualified_observations.observation: The sum tag is read as u64 then cast to usize before indexing; on a 32-bit usize, a tag exceeding its representable range can truncate before bounds check. Named row/product fields are inserted into a map without an explicit duplicate-name check, so duplicates can overwrite before the target decoder. The historical qualifier already records these two conditional format gaps; preserve its dedup scope.
findings_and_qualified_observations.condition: No proof of a deployed 32-bit strategic-web target, malformed server schema, accepted malformed concrete target row, or runtime failure. The shown production path checks array/product arity and many shapes; target decoder remains a separate owner. Do not claim all SATS/native semantics audited.
findings_and_qualified_observations.future_repair_direction: If native contract requires it, validate tag-width and named-field uniqueness at the adapter while preserving native valid option, enum, identity and byte semantics; first-result SQL response policy remains a separate caller question.

findings_and_qualified_observations.classification: bounded open contracts rather than new count
findings_and_qualified_observations.observation: PartyAction is a tagged intent enum with raw IDs, quantities and floats; the web layer branches between immediate dispatch and queued serialized intent, and approval reparses the payload before a planned route. The local redirect predicate admits a single-leading-slash value without backslash and is weaker than a complete native URI/header policy. Missing terrain and planning failures explicitly lead to the unplanned reducer option.
findings_and_qualified_observations.condition: No assumption that client intent alone is authority, that returned strings are unique action identity, that unplanned fallback is obsolete compatibility, or that redirect normalization is exploitable. Native authorization/approval, full parser/sink and fallback policy were not comprehensively inspected. 059 queue 493 retains separate query-error cause-erasure context.
findings_and_qualified_observations.future_repair_direction: If the owner confirms these are internal contracts rather than native ports, carry existing semantic IDs/errors through intent and invoke one canonical admission at the server. Preserve actual readiness, approval, URI and fallback behavior after design decisions.

lens_perspectives.assessment: Generated raw route points are copied into view and re-admitted at web use; trace all writers before choosing canonical admitted representation.
Wgs84CoordinateE7 already owns geographic axis checks; web conversion reuses it, while raw native and generated wire shape is a real boundary.
Planned-route validator rejects raw invalid WGS84; a corruption/other-writer route to web expect remains conditional, not established.
Both position functions use shortest spherical lengths yet direct longitude interpolation; seam case is the prior conditional queue item.
Validator relates point count, endpoints, distance, duration, weather and spans; do not infer whole-route invariant enforcement for unread writers.
Route and schema coordinate owners require cross-boundary decisions; generated DTO is not itself an editable owner.
Server and web independently calculate route position; retain shared-contract question without claiming divergent output for ordinary routes.
Keep current route timing, ordering, approved-action routing and explicit missing-terrain/planner fallback policy subject to owner decision; no repair performed.
PartyAction already pairs variants with payloads; action kind is a coarse category, not the unique authority discriminator.
Generated SATS derives and serde-tagged enum are boundary code; scoped reads do not establish removable boilerplate or macro semantics.
Separate checked WGS84 axes and unbounded abstract coordinates are intentional distinct uses in shown producer; generated raw points remain native wire.
Protocol keys and reducer names are adapter-facing; internal errors/action labels require caller and server-owner tracing before consolidating; 059 queue 493 is existing cause-erasure question.
Geographic scaling, route bounds, minutes and distance are named/validated in shown owners; 32-bit tag narrowing is target-dependent existing qualifier, not blanket literal defect.
